title: Canary busts and flight recorder runbook draft
summary: Notes from recent incidents where a canary rollout caused unexpected GPU pool saturation and P99 latency spikes. This doc sketches a fast triage playbook and a "flight recorder" instrumentation pattern to capture causality when canaries interact with autoscaler and cache behavior.
detection_signals: Primary signals we saw: sudden p99(ms) delta on /v1/generate for model-family X (hosted dedicated pool), surge in gpu_utilization per-node from 40%->95% within 3m, a drop in prefix cache hit-rate (KV hits/req) and an increase in avg tokens/sec per request. Alerts: alert_high_pool_latency (fired), autoscaler_scale_up_hotloop (fired), per-tenant-evictions (saw transient evictions).
timeline: T-0: Canary weight increased from 1%->10% at 03:12 UTC. T+2m: p99 on model X rose from 180ms->980ms. T+3m: autoscaler began rapid node provisioning—several nodes boot but failed healthchecks. T+9m: evictions observed in pool; fallback routing started hitting model-variant Y. T+18m: Oncall paused rollout, manually set canary weight to 0 and applied temporary circuit-breaker for the tenant. Service recovered to baseline by T+28m.
immediate_mitigation: 1) Pause canary rollout (set canary weight 0). 2) Apply per-tenant QPS limit in edge router for the canary tenant: nginx route limit or gateway quota. 3) If autoscaler hot-looping, increase scale cooldown to 300s and cap max-burst to +2 nodes. 4) If nodes failing healthchecks, cordon and drain suspicious nodes, reimage if kernel/GPU driver issues present. 5) Open an emergency revert PR for the model-variant change if rollout includes a behavior change.
runbook_draft: Overview: This is a short runbook for SREs to contain canary-induced GPU pool saturation. Steps: 1) Run quick-checks (see Quick Checks). 2) Identify whether incident originated from production canary: query rollout service for active canaries in last 30m. 3) If canary detected, scale canary down to 0% immediately and rate-limit its tenant traffic. 4) Inspect autoscaler events: prometheus query 'rate(autoscaler_events_total[5m])' and check for 'scale_up' flapping; temporarily set autoscaler.cooldown = 300s. 5) If prefix/KV cache hit-rate dropped > 20% concurrently, revert any cache keyspace changes and enable aggressive prewarm for hot tenants. 6) If noisy tenant detected, evict with eviction-policy=graceful and add temporary affinity isolation tag to the tenant so requests route to isolated pool. 7) Collect flight recorder artifacts (see Flight Recorder Design) before deleting logs. 8) After containment, run synthetic traffic against pool to validate p99 and kv hit-rate. 9) Re-enable canary only with additional telemetry and throttles.
flight_recorder_design: Goal: capture minimal, high-signal traces for a sampled subset of requests during a canary rollout so we can correlate request patterns with autoscaler and GPU metrics. Elements: - Request header 'X-Flight-Id' injected by rollout controller when weight changes; SREs can turn sampling ON by setting rollout.debug=true. - Per-request lightweight trace: trace_id, tenant_id, model_variant, tokens_in, kv_cache_hits, kv_cache_miss_count, queue_time_ms, decode_time_ms, node_id, gpu_mem_usage_mb. - Store sampled traces in a short-retention hot store (Loki with 7d retention + BigQuery export for postmortem). - Sampling policy: default 0.1% global, 10% for canary-tagged tenants when rollout.weight > 0. - Endpoint for on-demand capture: POST /debug/flight-recorder/start?duration=300s that autoscaler or SREs can call to increase sampling for 5m. Implementation notes: keep payload < 1KB, redact PII, include a 'reason' tag (canary, autoscale, manual), ensure tracing code path is no-op when sampling is OFF.
reproducer_steps: Non-prod repro plan: 1) Create synthetic canary tenant with model X. 2) Throttle token generation to simulate bursty user behavior (use load-generator to replay 50 simultaneous long requests with high prefix divergence). 3) Start canary weight at 10% and run for 10m. 4) Observe autoscaler and pool behavior, capture flight-recorder traces. 5) Iterate by toggling cache prewarm and binding canary to isolated affinity pool. Note: reproduce on a smaller pool first to avoid billing surprises.

quick_checks: Commands & queries: - Check active canaries: curl -s 'https://rollouts.internal/api/v1/active?since=30m' - GPU utilization by pool: prometheus 'avg_over_time(gpu_utilization_percent{pool="dedicated-1"}[5m])' - Per-node health: kubectl get nodes -l pool=dedicated-1 -o wide; check kubelet and nvidia-driver logs. - KV cache hit-rate: prometheus 'sum(kv_cache_hits)/sum(kv_cache_requests) by (pool, tenant)' - Autoscaler events: kubectl logs deployment/autoscaler --since=30m | tail -200 - Grafana panel: dedicated-pool-overview (p95 latency, gpu_util, kv_hit_rate, evictions).
notes_to_self: Unresolved: why did autoscaler fail healthcheck on new nodes? Check AMI/driver mismatch with runtime; look for GPU driver upgrades coincident with deploy. Also: consider adding 'min-serving-capacity' per-tenant to avoid eviction cascades from small canaries. Keep runbook short and prescriptive; link to this draft from incident playbook index.
